previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 20%), COPD, type 2 diabetes, hepatitis C, and crack lung was admitted for acute gastroenteritis following ingestion of undercooked chicken, presenting with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and high fever. He developed hypotension and tachycardia, with clinical worsening prompting broad-spectrum antibiotics and fluid resuscitation, which led to transient fluid overload and decompensated heart failure. His course was complicated by acute kidney injury and markedly elevated liver enzymes, both attributed to congestive hepatopathy from impaired cardiac output. Imaging showed stable chronic lung disease with apical infiltrates, treated as community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin. He improved with cautious diuresis, returning to his dry weight of 88.4 kg, with normalization of renal and liver function. He was discharged to extended care on his prior heart failure regimen with plans for outpatient follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ M h/o nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (LVEF 20% echo ___, DM 2, COPD, schizophrenia, polysubstance abuse 
presenting with shortness of breath and a episode of chest pain 
after use of crack cocaine.

# Shortness of breath: Patient reports crack cocaine use until 
5PM the day before admission presented complaining of dyspnea. 
Given prior admissions with decompensated pulmonary disease 
precipitated by crack cocaine use COPD/ILD flare is most likely. 
Alternative etiologies include CHF exacerbation, although CXR 
and physical exam are not markedly supportive of this diagnosis, 
and patient is at reported dry weight. The patient was given 
some IV Lasix. His breathing improved, and he was able to 
tolerate room air w/o NC with sats >90%. He began to feel it was 
easier to breath. He continued to have his baseline cough 
productive of minimal white foamy sputum, which improved with 
nebulizers and cough drops.

ACS is also possible given TropT of 0.09, although EKG is not 
consistent with acute ishcemia and TropT may be elevated ___ to 
ARF. Will evaluate as below.

# ___: Although cocaine use may precipitate AMI, patient's 
presentation and chest pain is not typical for ACS. Chest pain 
was very transient and was not the main reason for presentation. 
TropT is slightly elevated above baseline (0.3-0.5) but this is 
likely attributable to ARF. EKG did not show any worrisome 
changes. Nonetheless, patient was started on a heparin gtt in 
the ED with intent to ___. His troponins and CK-MB trended 
down, and we stoped heparin ggt after 3 sets of CEs. We 
increased his atorvastatin to 80 mg. Telemetry showed one run of 
25 beats of Ventricular Tachycardia, which self-terminated. This 
has been noted before on prior admissions. He was referred to 
return to his outpatient cardiologist for further management and 
consideration of future ICD placement.

# Nonischemic Cardiomyopathy and systolic heart failure: Patient 
had a recent admission with decompensation of CHF that required 
adjustment of diuretic regimen. At admission he was at his dry 
weight but had some clinical signs of mild volume overload. He 
was given some lasix, and his breathing imroved. He was not felt 
to be in a CHF exacerbation during this admission. Lisinopril 
was held for 1 dose bc Cr was elevated.  

# COPD/Crack Pneumonitis: Patient reports recent crack use until 
5PM yesterday with subsequent dyspnea. Given prior challenges 
with ILD ___ to crack use and likely contribution to current 
presentation, will proceed with symptomatic treatment. The 
patient was given albuterol and ipratropium nebulizers PRN, and 
continued on home fluticasone/salmeterol. His breathing improved 
and he was able to tolerate breathing with O2sats > 92% without 
NC. It was not felt that steroid treatment was ncessary during 
this admission. 
 
# ARF and Hyperkalemia: Patient presents with elevated K to 5.6 
and Cr of 1.5 (which is above recent nadir of 1.0) although Cr 
on discharge was 1.4. Lisinopril was initially held, and Cr 
trended down. Kayexalate was given with good response. 

# Type II DM: Continue insulin and SSI in house  

# CKD: renally dose medications.  

# HLD: Atorvastatin 80 mg as above can reduce to 20mg after ___
 
# Smoking cessation: Nicotine patch  

# Hypertension - Continue home carvedilol and lisinopril.  

# Schizophrenia - Patient is not currently being managed as an  
outpatient with medication. Denies hallucinations at this time.

# FEN: IVFs / replete lytes prn / regular diet  
# PPX: heparin SQ, bowel regimen
